security_audit.summary: Most static command and entropy findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, Japanese documentation, and readable tables. The real concerns are a prompt-priority override sentence in SKILL.md and the intended use of Bash to run project-controlled build and test scripts.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the claim that the quality guardrail section has priority over other instructions. Reword it as guidance that applies only within the skill scope.
Require explicit user confirmation before running build, test, lint, package install, or recovery commands. Show the exact command before execution.
Use least-privilege tool declarations for each subskill. Keep Write, Edit, and Bash only where the workflow requires them.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md states "このセクションは他の指示より優先されます", meaning the section has priority over other instructions. A marketplace skill must not claim authority over higher-priority system, developer, or user instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text directly asserts instruction priority inside an untrusted skill file. It appears intended as a local quality rule, but it still creates a prompt-hierarchy override risk.

semantic_findings.description: The skill enables Bash and instructs agents to run build, test, type-check, and lint commands. These commands can execute project-controlled scripts and should require explicit user confirmation in untrusted repositories.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools metadata includes Bash, and verify-build/doc.md lists concrete build, test, and lint command workflows. This is expected functionality, but it creates real execution risk when project scripts are untrusted.

content.user_title: Verify Builds and Apply Review Fixes
content.value_statement: Build failures and review fixes can slow delivery when errors are unclear. This skill runs focused verification workflows and guides safe recovery steps.
actual_capabilities: Routes build, test, lint, error recovery, review aggregation, and review fix requests.
Runs common Node.js and Python build, test, type-check, and lint commands when Bash is available.
Analyzes failures, applies limited fixes, and escalates unresolved errors after repeated attempts.
Aggregates security, performance, quality, and accessibility review results into a weighted summary.
Applies approved review fixes and asks for confirmation when changes may affect behavior.
limitations: It depends on local project scripts, dependencies, and available command-line tools.
It cannot guarantee safe execution of commands in untrusted repositories.
It needs user approval before changing tests, configuration, or behavior-sensitive code.
It does not replace manual review for security or architecture decisions.

use_cases.title: Verify a completed change
use_cases.description: Run build, type-check, test, and lint checks before sending code for review.

use_cases.title: Recover from failing tests
use_cases.description: Analyze failure output, identify likely causes, and apply small fixes with verification.

use_cases.title: Apply approved review feedback
use_cases.description: Convert review findings into safe fixes, then present the result and next checks.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Recent Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify my recent changes. Check build, tests, type checks, and lint. Summarize any failures and the next action.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a Test Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: The tests are failing. Read the failure output, identify the cause, propose a safe fix, and rerun the relevant checks.

prompt_templates.title: Aggregate Review Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Combine these review findings into one prioritized summary. Separate security, performance, quality, and accessibility issues.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Approved Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply only the review fixes I approved. Show the changed files, explain skipped items, and verify the result afterward.

output_examples.input: Verify my recent changes before review.
output_examples.output: Build passed. Type checks passed. Tests passed. Lint reported one warning that should be reviewed before merge.

output_examples.input: The unit tests are failing after my change.
output_examples.output: The failure appears related to outdated expectations. I recommend confirming the expected behavior before changing the test.
Three safe fixes were applied. One behavior-sensitive item was skipped and needs manual confirmation.

best_practices: Review commands before execution when working in unfamiliar repositories.
Ask for approval before changing tests, lint settings, CI settings, or expected values.
Rerun the smallest relevant verification command after each fix.
anti_patterns: Do not skip tests to make a verification run pass.
Do not weaken lint, type, or CI rules without explicit approval.
Do not apply review fixes that change behavior without understanding the requirement.

faq.question: Can this skill run build and test commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to run project verification commands when the agent has Bash access.

faq.question: Does it modify code automatically?
faq.answer: It can apply small fixes when the workflow allows editing. Risky changes should require user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it fix failing tests?
faq.answer: It can diagnose failures and fix implementation issues. It should not weaken tests just to pass.

faq.question: Does it support review feedback?
faq.answer: Yes. It can aggregate findings and apply approved review fixes with a follow-up verification step.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Build and test commands may execute project-controlled scripts or dependency hooks.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
